def lex_max_graph(d):
    """
    Construct the lexicographically largest adjacency matrix of a simple
    undirected graph with a prescribed degree sequence.

    Input: d is a list of n integers with 1 <= n <= 40 and 0 <= d[i] <= n-1.
    A simple graph on vertices 0..n-1 (undirected, no self-loops, no
    multiple edges) realizes d if vertex i has degree exactly d[i].

    Encode a graph as its adjacency matrix written as n strings, where row
    i is a string of n characters whose j-th character is '1' if edge
    {i, j} is present and '0' otherwise (the matrix is symmetric and every
    diagonal character is '0').

    Among all graphs that realize d, return the encoding whose row-major
    concatenation row0 + row1 + ... + row(n-1) is lexicographically
    largest, as the list [row0, ..., row(n-1)]. If no simple graph
    realizes d, return the empty list []. The lexicographically largest
    realization is unique, so the output is fully determined.

    Note: the number of graphs on 40 vertices is astronomical, so
    enumeration is hopeless, and greedily taking any edge whose two
    endpoints still need degree is wrong (it can get stuck even when a
    realization exists).

    >>> lex_max_graph([1, 1])
    ['01', '10']
    >>> lex_max_graph([2, 1, 1, 2])
    ['0101', '1000', '0001', '1010']
    >>> lex_max_graph([1, 1, 1])
    []
    """
